clue.text: Every known beer (as well as roll) often passes a politician's lips

parts.note: every one is all of them
piss is a coarse slang name for weak beer, so beer known by that name
a plain synonym for and
to roll something up is to wind it

explanation.surface: A politician seems to be forever drinking every beer going, plus a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL PISS AND WIND is British slang for someone who is all bluster and no substance; the clue enjoys the idea that both liquids and gas escape a politician's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes empty, boastful talk, exactly the bluster that routinely comes out of politicians' mouths.

clue.text: Key party clique showing devotion

parts.note: A is a musical key
a do is a party
a ring is a closed group of insiders

explanation.surface: A key-swapping party where one group seems devoted to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them devotedly, so adoring describes devotion.

clue.text: Mae West: "Flies are undone — first sign of Viagra inside"

indicators.note: that opening letter goes within the rearranged letters
undone flies are open and disordered, so the letters of flies are are rearranged

parts.note: these two words are taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the drug's name is taken

parts.note: the drug's name, of which only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: The actress Mae West quips about a man's open trouser fly and a drug taking effect.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West was RAF slang for an inflatable life jacket, named for the actress's bust.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable life jacket called a Mae West is a device that saves people from drowning.

clue.text: Cyclops on date with priestess gets married in a manner of speaking

parts.note: the one-eyed giant gives the setter's pseudonym, and the setter is I
Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth

explanation.surface: The setter on a date with a priestess speaks of getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression, a characteristic way of saying something in a language.

clue.text: Familiar critic snapping "Arse! Behind!" (not live)

indicators.note: snapping breaks the letters apart so they can be reset
not tells us the word for living is taken away from the letters

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be mixed
taken as written, letters to be mixed
to be is to exist, so to live

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued critic snaps rude words about someone's backside, though not on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan Morley was a well-known British theatre critic, called here by first name, as a familiar would.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan Morley, the theatre critic, is referred to by his first name in the way friends address one another.

clue.text: Nun was once a month 'confection'

parts.note: Nov is the calendar abbreviation for November
an ice is a frozen sweet confection

explanation.surface: A nun spent a month making a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationer in a religious order, the stage every professed nun passes through first.

clue.text: Sort of farce that symbolises our government

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trouser-dropping stage comedy from the ... Theatre
second meaning: the London street of ministries, standing for the civil service and government

explanation.walkthrough: The satirical point is that British government itself is a farce.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall is both the theatre famous for bedroom farces and the street whose ministries embody British government.

clue.text: Jimmy's fixes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to Jimmy Nail, the Geordie actor and singer

explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy looks like the burglar's crowbar or a verb; it is Jimmy Nail, a British actor and singer.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fix it in place with metal pins, and Nail's is the actor's possessive surname.

clue.text: 'New' Church of England shortly to get involved in gay movement operation

indicators.note: the abbreviations become mixed up with the other letters
movement shifts the letters of gay around

parts.note: the short form of Church of England is CE
the word gay taken as written, its letters to be moved about

explanation.surface: The Church of England, newly modernised, joins the gay rights movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Agency means action or operation, the means by which something is done.

clue.text: In no position to score, Dicky's on the verge

parts.note: dicky means unwell or unreliable, much like off
the verge of a road is its side

explanation.surface: A sexually frustrated man called Dicky can't score and is close to breaking point.
explanation.walkthrough: The football sense is the definition: a player offside cannot legally score.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a player in an offside position cannot legally receive the ball to score a goal.

clue.text: Effecting public cover-up about living outside Mile End

indicators.note: the rearranged living sits outside, wrapping the last letter of mile
about here means around in a jumble, so the letters of living are rearranged

parts.note: the word living is taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here the last of mile; Mile End is also a London district

parts.note: the word mile, whose last letter is used

explanation.surface: A public body hushes up the truth about how people live outside Mile End, an East London district.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a covering, so veiling something is concealing or covering it up in public view.

clue.text: Someone who can't get off with Simon turning to flipping relative killer

indicators.note: turning churns the letters of Simon into a new order

parts.note: the name taken as written, its letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: flipping turns the brother-killer's name back to front

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man who can't get off with Simon turns to murdering a relative in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: To get off here means to fall asleep, not to make a romantic conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: An insomniac is a person who is chronically unable to fall asleep at night.

clue.text: As used by 'goers' at e.g. outdoor rock festivals?

definitions.meaning: not festival-goers in general but people who need to go, to the toilet
open-air music festivals rely on portable chemical toilets

explanation.walkthrough: An Elsan is a British brand of chemical toilet, the name used generically for the portable loos at campsites and festivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable chemical lavatories of this brand are the standard sanitation at open-air concerts.

clue.text: Blow delivered by hand on leader

parts.note: to hand something over is to give it
the head is the leader of an organisation

explanation.surface: A punch thrown with the fist at the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Blow is not a punch but slang for oral sex, which the answer also names.
explanation.definitionFit: In vulgar slang a blow job and giving head are the same sexual act.

clue.text: End of Bush (hey! hey!) without vote of the rabble

indicators.note: only the closing letter of Bush is taken

parts.note: the US president's name, of which only the closing letter is used

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the cries surround the vote

parts.note: oi is a rough British shout for attention
the same shout again
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Jeering crowds shout at the end of George Bush's term, a vote denied to the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi, Greek for the many, is a dismissive name for the common people or the masses.

clue.text: Surprise passer-by with street shag

parts.note: a way is a road or street, as in Broadway
both are slang for having sex

explanation.surface: Someone startles a pedestrian by having sex in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To waylay is to ambush or intercept someone as they go along their route.

clue.text: State of French agreements commandeered by Tarzan supporter

indicators.note: the French agreements are taken inside the jungle creeper

parts.note: Tarzan swings from lianas, jungle vines
oui is French for yes

explanation.surface: The French state's treaties seized by a backer of Tarzan.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the United States, once French territory.

clue.text: Degenerative state of Damien Hirst's ultimate energy-absorbing composition

indicators.note: a composition is an arrangement, so the letters are put together in a new order
absorbing means the energy letter is taken in to join the pool of letters

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of Hirst

parts.note: the name Hirst, the possessive linking it to its ultimate letter
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Private Eye sniping that one of Damien Hirst's energy-sapping artworks shows his decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges DAMIEN, the T ending Hirst and the E it takes in. 'composition' looks like an artwork by Hirst, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is a progressive decline in memory and reasoning, a condition that worsens over time.

clue.text: Clubby thing possibly having sex (head, at any rate) with Schwarzenegger

indicators.note: the head of the word sex is its opening letter

parts.note: the word sex, of which only the first letter is taken
Arnold Schwarzenegger is widely nicknamed Arnie

explanation.surface: A nightclub type fancies sex with the action star Schwarzenegger, or at least oral sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarnie is British slang for a sandwich, and a club sandwich is one, hence 'Clubby thing possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a kind of stacked sandwich, so a sarnie may be one.

clue.text: Fanny's weightlifting technique

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British vulgar slang for female genitals
second meaning: the Olympic lift raising the bar overhead in one motion

explanation.walkthrough: Fanny reads as a woman's name with a hobby; in British slang it is a body part, and snatch is coarse slang for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Snatch is both vulgar slang for the vulva and the name of an Olympic weightlifting lift.

clue.text: Spring on Barbarian — good, splendidly tackled!

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
the Huns were barbarian invaders

explanation.surface: Rugby commentary: a player pounces on a Barbarians man and makes a cracking tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbarians are a famous invitation rugby team; tackle is also slang for male genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Well hung is slang for a man with large genitals, his tackle being impressive.

clue.text: Blanket Girl gobbles up Rene

indicators.note: the girl swallows the man's name inside her

parts.note: gal is a casual word for a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the French man's name taken as written, then read upwards

explanation.surface: A girl wrapped in a blanket devours a man called Rene.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket statement is a general one, covering all cases without distinction.

clue.text: Swear Spielberg film with implausible ending is rather feeble

parts.note: to eff is to swear, from the euphemism eff off
ET is Spielberg's alien film

indicators.note: ending takes the closing letter of implausible

parts.note: the word implausible, of which only the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A critic swears that a Spielberg film with an unbelievable ending is weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means weak, ineffectual or lacking vigour, an over-refined feebleness.

clue.text: Member clutched by top notch work-mate

indicators.note: the member is held inside the letters for top notch

parts.note: first-rate is A1, with the one written as the letter I
a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: A colleague grips some top-quality body part at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Work-mate splits: work gives the last two letters and mate is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, used in English as a casual term for a pal.

clue.text: State aid bungled by House

indicators.note: bungled letters are messed up and put in a new order

parts.note: the word aid taken as written, its letters to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A state aid programme botched by the House of Representatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA, in the north-west.

clue.text: Organisation man complimentary to our Brenda and Brian (relatively speaking)

parts.note: a complimentary ticket is a free one
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, and relatively speaking she is a mother, ma
Brian is the Eye's nickname for Prince Charles, who relatively speaking is her son

explanation.surface: A man in a secret society flatters the Queen and Prince Charles, the Eye's Brenda and Brian, and their family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively speaking' tells you to describe the two royals by their family relationship: mother and son.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason belongs to the fraternal society often just called the Organisation or the Brotherhood.

clue.text: Misses 'Monday disease'

parts.note: AIDS is the immune-system disease

explanation.walkthrough: Misses is not failing to hit but unmarried women, the old sense of maid.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old word for an unmarried girl, and Miss is the title for such a woman.

clue.text: Prince's name for a drug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the familiar form of Charles, as Prince Charles is called

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the singer Prince renaming himself, but it is about the royal Prince Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is both a pet form of the name Charles and long-standing slang for cocaine.

clue.text: Not much up top, dropping heroin — a state of non-existence

indicators.note: dropping means the drug's letter falls out of the phrase

parts.note: a balding head has thin hair

explanation.surface: A balding man gives up heroin and drifts into oblivion.
explanation.walkthrough: Things that vanish into thin air cease to exist, the sense used here.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing into thin air means disappearing completely, so thin air stands for nothingness.

clue.text: Knacker of the Yard's money-raiser?

definitions.meaning: Inspector Knacker of the Yard is Private Eye's stock Scotland Yard detective, and a knacker is also a testicle
a charity dance held to raise funds

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a policeman's knacker is literally one of his balls, while the annual police ball raises money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The police charity dance is a fund-raising event, and knacker is slang for a testicle.
